title: Mere man cannot bear infinite curse-weight
source_text: VII. Neque etiam id potuit simplex & nudus homo, qui oneri maledictionis divinae succubuisset, nec potuisset ferre poenas aequivalentes iis quas totum genus humanum commeruerat, ad quod vis & dignitas infinita requirebatur. Unde sequitur talem Vadem Deum & hominem simul omnino esse debuisse.
pass_a_gloss: Nor could a mere and bare man do it, who would have sunk under the burden of the divine curse, nor could he bear penalties equivalent to those which the whole human race had deserved, for which infinite power and dignity were required. Hence it follows that such a Surety had to be altogether God and man at once.
pass_b_english: A bare man would sink under the divine curse and cannot equal the race’s desert.
The Surety must be both God and man.
